subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Cognitive Hierarchy Theory
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Cognitive Hierarchy Theory.

hook.text: A chess grandmaster thinks 15 moves ahead. A beginner thinks 2. Cognitive hierarchy says both are rational for their.

buildup.text: Camerer's cognitive hierarchy model assumes a distribution of thinking levels.

discovery.text: The model fits data better than Nash equilibrium in one-shot games. People don't assume others are perfectly rational.

twist.text: The distribution is Poisson-shaped with an average around 1.5 steps. Very few people think beyond level 3.

climax.text: In negotiations, estimate your opponent's thinking level. Match it and go one step further.

punchline.text: Think one step deeper than your opponent. No more, no less.

quiz.question: What does cognitive hierarchy theory assume about players?
options: All players think at the same level of depth
Players have different thinking depths and best-respond to lower levels
Only the smartest player can win any game

details.summary: Cognitive hierarchy theory proposes that players think in levels: level-0 players choose randomly, level-1 players best-respond to random play, level-2 players best-respond to level-1, and so on, with most people thinking only 1 to 2 levels deep.
details.whyItMatters: This theory explains why people do not play Nash equilibrium strategies in complex games. Most people only think a few steps ahead, creating predictable patterns that more sophisticated thinkers can exploit.
takeaways: Players are distributed across different levels of strategic thinking
Most people think only 1 to 2 levels deep in strategic situations
Level-k models predict behavior better than Nash equilibrium in many games

faq.question: How do you determine someone's level of thinking?
faq.answer: Experiments use games like the beauty contest, where players pick numbers and the closest to two-thirds of the average wins. Level-0 picks randomly around 50, level-1 picks 33, level-2 picks 22. Most people cluster around levels 1 and 2.

faq.question: Can you improve your level of strategic thinking?
faq.answer: Yes, through practice and awareness. Experienced game players, professional strategists, and people trained in game theory tend to think more levels deep. But even experts rarely exceed level 3 or 4 in complex real-world situations.
